patches.title: Codex: upload an explicit provider config.toml from CODEX_CONFIG_TOML_PATH
patches.score_effect: Indirect but universal: this is how every AgentSWE builder gets its provider, model, reasoning effort and [features] multi_agent=false. Without it the builder runs against the default OpenAI provider (run invalid, not merely different).
patches.upstream: Equivalent native feature since harbor 0.21.0 (Codex(config=<path|inline>)); not byte-identical (0.21 re-renders the TOML via toml.dumps). Not backported to 0.20.x.

patches.title: Terminus-2: pass session env through `env K=V tmux new-session` instead of `-e` (tmux < 3.2)
patches.score_effect: TerminalBench only (Terminus-2 starter/candidate). On task images with tmux 3.1c the upstream `-e` makes session start fail whenever extra_env is non-empty (AgentSWE always passes AGENTSWE_TB_*). Not reachable from the Lite tasks.

patches.title: Classify Codex 'stream disconnected before completion' as ApiConnectionClosedError
patches.score_effect: Changes only the exception class of a failed builder command. With builder resume enabled (the launcher of the paper's earlier Creation runs) such failures become resumable; with resume disabled (Lite) only result.json exception_type changes - both are caught by single_step and the Creation adapter withholds the phase either way.
patches.upstream: 0.23.0 only matches Claude Code's 'API Error: stream closed before completion': upstream candidate.

patches.title: Codex resume: resume the single root thread by id instead of `resume --last`
hunks: C7 resume "$(cat marker)" (+ output_path refactor, no-op)
patches.category: a (C4-C7); d (refactor parts of C7, C8)
patches.score_effect: Only on a resumed builder trial. `resume --last` can pick a sub-agent thread; the selector refuses unless exactly one root thread exists. With multi-agent disabled (Lite policy) both select the same thread.
patches.upstream: 0.23.0 still uses `resume --last`: upstream candidate (generic multi-agent bug).

patches.title: SingleStepTrial: opt-in in-place resume after transient API/network failures
patches.score_effect: Builder phase only, only when AGENTSWE_INFRA_RESUME_ENABLED=1 (set by the launcher of the paper's earlier Creation runs; NOT set for the Lite runs). With it disabled the behaviour equals upstream (ApiError subclasses NonZeroAgentExitCodeError and is recorded). Known quirks: each resume restarts the full agent timeout; agent_execution timing and AgentContext are overwritten by the last attempt; state file not finalised on a terminal non-infra error.
patches.upstream: No equivalent through 0.23.0 (job-level RetryConfig starts a fresh trial). Recommended: move into the AgentSWE Codex agent class.

patches.title: Claude Code: take ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL / ANTHROPIC_MODEL from the agent env
patches.score_effect: GLM-5.3 + Claude Code row only (provider routing; without it the harness talks to the default Anthropic endpoint/model).
patches.upstream: Equivalent since 0.21.0 (base URL) / 0.22.0 (ANTHROPIC_MODEL from agent env).

patches.title: Docker: no resources-override cpus for a main service whose task compose sets cpu_quota/cpu_period
patches.score_effect: None on scores; it decides whether an Editing Builder container starts at all. Every Editing task writes its Builder compose with cpu_quota=800000/cpu_period=100000 (the 8-CPU contract its builder_resources.py checks), and Harbor adds cpus=8 from task.toml. Docker Compose 2.40 sends cpus as NanoCPUs next to CpuPeriod, which the Docker daemon refuses (Conflicting options: Nano CPUs and CPU Period cannot both be set), so no Builder started there. Compose v2.5.0 ignores cpus: those Builders ran with quota/period only and NanoCPUs 0, which is what 0007 gives under every compose version. Composes without cpu_quota/cpu_period (all Creation and Optimization ones) still get cpus.
patches.upstream: Not checked against later Harbor releases; upstream candidate.
